# aibris v0.15.1

This patch release closes gaps in how guided review decides that an active
worktree has no recent Codex session, lets Orca-only users review active Orca
worktrees, and refuses Windows junction cache leaves. It contains fixes to
existing behavior and one additive receipt reason code.

## Highlights

- **Guided review sees sessions that started moments ago** (#627).
  - Before, guided review could reuse a Codex activity index up to 15 minutes
    old without reading the session stores, so a session started in that
    window did not lock its worktree. Guided review now refreshes the index
    every time. Unchanged session files are not read again.
  - Right before removing a guided active worktree, aibris refreshes again and
    re-derives activity with the same rules. It keeps the worktree when a
    member has a newer or recent session than the review saw, or when
    activity evidence is no longer available. The receipt records
    `activity_evidence_changed`, and the human output says why.
- **Relocated or unmounted session stores no longer read as "no activity"**
  (#623).
  - Before, a native Codex worktree whose `~/.codex/sessions` was a symlink to
    another directory, or whose `archived_sessions` pointed at an unmounted
    volume, could lose its recent-activity lock and become reviewable.
  - A Codex home now speaks for "no recent session" only when `sessions/` is a
    directory inside the home and `archived_sessions/` is either absent or a
    readable directory inside the home. Dangling symlinks, files, Windows
    junctions and other reparse points, and stores that cannot be listed
    keep active worktrees protected with `activity_evidence_unavailable`. The
    check repeats at lookup, so a cached index cannot bypass it. Native Codex
    and Orca worktrees follow the same rule.
- **Orca-only users can review active Orca worktrees** (#624). If you have
  never run the Codex CLI directly, the default `~/.codex` home has no session
  store. That proven absence now counts as zero activity for Orca worktrees,
  instead of locking them permanently. It applies only to the unconfigured
  default home; a missing `CODEX_HOME` or `AIBRIS_CODEX_HOMES` path (possibly
  a typo), a symlinked home, an archive-only home, or an unreadable store still
  keeps them locked.
- **Windows junction cache leaves are refused** (#611). A catalog cache whose
  leaf is a Windows junction or another reparse point is shown as skipped
  with `cache_leaf_symlink`, its bytes are left out of the selected total, and
  execution refuses it. Before, path removal would have deleted only the link
  while counting the target's bytes.

## Compatibility impact

- [x] **Compatible addition.**
  - New receipt reason code `activity_evidence_changed`. It appears in guided
    `--receipt-file` receipts when the pre-mutation barrier refuses a unit.
    Guided execution is not available with `--json`, and JSON plans never
    contain this code.
  - `cache_leaf_symlink` now also covers Windows junctions and other reparse
    points. Its name and meaning for symlinks are unchanged.
  - No flag, field, or enum value was removed or renamed, and
    `schema_version` stays `1`.

## Upgrade and migration

No flag migration is required.

```bash
brew upgrade aibris
# or (Unix):
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sungjunlee/aibris/refs/heads/main/install.sh | bash -s -- v0.15.1
# or (Windows PowerShell):
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sungjunlee/aibris/refs/heads/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

- The Codex activity cache changed revision. An older cache is discarded and
  rebuilt the next time it is read.
- If your `~/.codex/sessions` or `archived_sessions` is a symlink to another
  directory or volume, active Codex worktrees now stay protected in guided
  review. Orphaned worktrees are still cleaned by the classic plan. Recovering
  activity evidence through such a symlink is tracked in #634.

## Safety

- Every earlier safeguard is unchanged: the single deletion gate, dry-run and
  confirmation, `--risky`, active-worktree protection, agent-state proof and
  grace, re-verification at the mutation boundary, and overlap safety.
- Fail-closed narrowing: relocated, dangling, or unreadable session stores
  now lock active native Codex worktrees in guided review, as they already
  did for Orca worktrees.
- The one relaxation (#624) applies only to the unconfigured default home
  when both of its session stores provably do not exist, and only to Orca
  worktrees; it is re-proven at lookup and at the mutation barrier.
- Known limitations, tracked for follow-up:
  - Session activity uses each session's start time. Work that continues in
    an existing session after review is not seen as newer activity (#636).
    Git changes are still caught by the dirty-worktree and reflog checks.
  - Activity evidence is not recovered through a relocated session store, and
    a Windows `~/.codex` that is itself a junction is not yet proven to fail
    closed (#634).
  - Classic `--include-active-worktrees` selection does not use the session
    activity barrier, as before.

## Windows status

Native Windows CI now also runs the restored cleaner command authority and
execution tests through a re-exec fake-tool fixture (#602), the cache-leaf
junction refusal tests (#611), and the Codex `sessions/` junction activity
test (#623), alongside the full `internal/safedelete`, `internal/pathidentity`,
and `internal/testutil` packages and the production PowerShell installer
tests. Real vendor agent worktree layouts on Windows, end-to-end delete
mutation, and native arm64 execution remain experimental and unmeasured. See
`docs/WINDOWS.md`.
